disorders_and_pests.conducive_weather: Cool (12-18°C), high relative humidity (>85%), prolonged wet foliage from fog or drizzle
disorders_and_pests.distinguishing_features: Water-soaked irregular brown lesions on leaf tips or margins; delicate white powdery/velvety mold ring under leaf surface in humid mornings; foul rotting odor in severe cases.
cultural_controls: Use certified disease-free seed tubers from trusted hill seed farms (e.g. ICAR-CPRI Kufri Jyoti / Kufri Himalini).
Maintain wide terrace row spacing (60 cm) to facilitate air circulation and rapid canopy drying.
Avoid overhead sprinkling; irrigate into soil furrows in late morning.
Ensure high hilling/earthing-up to physically shield growing tubers from washed-down spores.
physical_controls: Immediately clip and burn or deeply bury early infected lower leaves (do NOT add to compost pile).
Cut foliage (haulm killing) 10-12 days before tuber harvest if late blight is active to prevent spores touching tubers during digging.
biological_controls: Preventive foliar spray of Trichoderma viride or Pseudomonas fluorescens (5 g/L) during early vegetative stages.
safe_treatments: Preventive application of Bordeaux mixture (1%) or Copper oxychloride (2.5 g/L) before continuous wet/foggy spells as permitted in hill agriculture guidelines.
disorders_and_pests.escalation_criteria: If more than 15-20% of terrace foliage is rapidly browning within 48 hours under persistent mountain mist, report to local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) plant clinic immediately.
sources: ICAR-CPRI Shimla Late Blight Forecasting & Management Bulletin

disorders_and_pests.conducive_weather: Dry sunny days with cool humid nights (typical autumn terrace conditions)
disorders_and_pests.distinguishing_features: Talcum-powder-like white spots that expand to coat entire upper leaf surfaces; affected leaves turn chlorotic yellow, curl upward, and dry out prematurely.
cultural_controls: Select resistant varieties (e.g., Pea varieties VL Aakash / VL Matar 8 from ICAR-VPKAS).
Avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer which creates dense, succulent foliage susceptible to infection.
Plant with adequate spacing facing the morning sun to ensure prompt drying of dew.
physical_controls: Carefully pinch and remove lower infected leaves showing early white powder patches.
biological_controls: Foliar spray with Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus subtilis formulation.
Diluted fresh cow milk spray (1 part milk to 9 parts water) exposed to sunlight produces free radicals that disrupt fungal mycelium.
safe_treatments: Potassium bicarbonate or wettable sulfur (2 g/L) applied early in the morning. Avoid sulfur application during rare hot days (>28°C).
disorders_and_pests.escalation_criteria: If powdery growth spreads to developing pea pods or cauliflower heads during flowering/curd stage.
sources: ICAR-VPKAS Almora Package of Practices for Hill Vegetables

disorders_and_pests.conducive_weather: Mild sunny spells in spring and post-monsoon hill seasons
disorders_and_pests.distinguishing_features: Irregular large holes chewed through leaves leaving only tough veins (skeletonization); clusters of bright yellow eggs on underside of leaves; green hairy caterpillars with dark spots; dark green fecal pellets (frass) lodged in leaf axils.
cultural_controls: Intercrop with strong aromatic repellent plants like garlic or coriander along terrace edges.
Plant Indian mustard (Brassica juncea) as a trap crop around cabbage beds: caterpillars prefer mustard, keeping main crops clean.
physical_controls: Handpick and destroy egg clusters and visible feeding caterpillars every morning.
Install fine insect mesh netting (40 mesh) over terrace hoops from early transplanting.
biological_controls: Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt var. kurstaki) at 1.5-2.0 g/L in the evening; highly selective against caterpillars without harming pollinators or bees.
Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE 5%) or cold-pressed neem oil (5 ml/L + drop of mild soap) as an anti-feedant.
safe_treatments: Local wood ash dusted over wet dew-covered leaves in early morning acts as an abrasive deterrent.
disorders_and_pests.escalation_criteria: If inner central growing head (heart) of cabbage or cauliflower curd is breached by bore-in larvae.
sources: Dr. Y.S. Parmar UHF Solan IPM in Mountain Cruciferous Crops

disorders_and_pests.conducive_weather: Dry cool periods, protected microclimates, absence of driving rain
disorders_and_pests.distinguishing_features: Dense colonies of tiny soft-bodied green, greyish, or black pear-shaped insects huddled under leaves; sticky, sweet honeydew excretion causing secondary black sooty mold; crinkled, cupped young leaves.
cultural_controls: Avoid over-fertilizing with quick-release nitrogen which stimulates aphid population explosions.
Encourage native predatory beneficials (ladybird beetles, hoverfly larvae, lacewings) by planting hill flowering borders (fennel, sweet alyssum).
physical_controls: Dislodge dense colonies using a firm jet of cool water directed at leaf undersides in the morning.
Install yellow sticky cards (1 per 10 m² terrace bed) suspended 10 cm above plant canopy to trap winged migrants.
biological_controls: Conserve Coccinella septempunctata (7-spotted ladybird beetle) adults and alligator-like larvae commonly found on mountain terraces.
Spray Verticillium lecanii or Beauveria bassiana (5 g/L) under humid conditions.
safe_treatments: Mild potassium horticultural soap spray (10-15 ml/L) or neem oil (3-5 ml/L) to dissolve insect protective cuticle.
disorders_and_pests.escalation_criteria: If aphids act as vectors transmitting mosaic viruses (mottled yellow foliage, severe leaf curling) across potato seed crops.

disorders_and_pests.conducive_weather: Warm, sunny, dry days in early mountain spring when seedlings emerge
disorders_and_pests.distinguishing_features: Numerous tiny round 'shot-hole' perforations (1-2 mm) peppered across leaves; tiny shiny black or bronze beetles that jump vigorously like fleas when approached.
cultural_controls: Maintain consistently moist seedbed during the first 3 weeks; flea beetles dislike wet, cool conditions.
Use thick organic straw mulch immediately around seedlings.
physical_controls: Keep beds covered with floating row cover (agrifleece) from sowing until seedlings develop 5-6 true leaves.
Dust fine wood ash or diatomaceous earth onto damp morning foliage.
biological_controls: Beneficial entomopathogenic nematodes (Heterorhabditis bacteriophora) applied to terrace soil to parasitize overwintered larvae.
safe_treatments: Neem oil spray (5 ml/L) with mild surfactant applied every 5 days during seedling vulnerability window.
disorders_and_pests.escalation_criteria: If cotyledons of newly emerged seedlings have >30% shot-hole damage before first true leaves form.

disorders_and_pests.conducive_weather: Cool spring soil with decaying vegetative residue
disorders_and_pests.distinguishing_features: Young seedlings or transplants severed cleanly right at or just beneath the soil level overnight; fallen wilted seedling lying beside intact root; fat, grey-brown caterpillar curled in a 'C' shape hidden 2-5 cm deep in soil near severed plant.
cultural_controls: Clear and turn terrace topsoil 2 weeks before planting to expose dormant larvae to mountain birds and solar UV.
Keep planting beds completely free of weeds and green residue for 10-14 days prior to sowing.
physical_controls: Install physical seedling collars: place 5-7 cm tall cylinders made of stiff cardboard or recycled plastic bottles pressed 2 cm into soil around each transplant stem.
Hand-dig around freshly severed plants at dawn to locate and eliminate the curled caterpillar hiding within a 10 cm radius.
biological_controls: Soil drench with Steinernema carpocapsae nematodes or Beauveria bassiana.
safe_treatments: Crushed neem cake (Azadirachta indica seed cake) incorporated at 50 g/m² during terrace bed preparation.
disorders_and_pests.escalation_criteria: If more than 10% of new transplants are felled within the first 3 nights.
sources: ICAR-CPRI & SKUAST Mountain Soil Entomology Guide

disorders_and_pests.scientific_name: Pythium spp. / Rhizoctonia solani / Fusarium spp.
disorders_and_pests.conducive_weather: Cold, soggy, compacted soil with poor drainage; overwatering in low sunshine terraces
disorders_and_pests.distinguishing_features: Seeds rot before emergence; newly emerged seedlings pinch thin, become water-soaked and brown at soil line, collapsing flat onto the ground; root system is dark, mushy, and devoid of white feeding hairs.
cultural_controls: Never plant into cold, waterlogged, heavy clay soil; construct 20 cm raised terrace beds with coarse sand and compost.
Avoid sowing seeds too deep where cold soil delays emergence.
Allow upper 2 cm of soil to dry slightly between irrigations.
physical_controls: Solarize terrace seedbeds with clear plastic film for 3 weeks prior to spring planting if sunny weather permits.
Discard collapsed seedlings along with adjacent soil immediately.
biological_controls: Seed treatment with Trichoderma harzianum or Trichoderma viride powder (4-5 g per kg seed) before planting.
Enrich farmyard manure with Trichoderma 15 days before soil application.
safe_treatments: Soil drench with copper hydroxide or bio-fungicide slurry at base of remaining healthy seedlings.
disorders_and_pests.escalation_criteria: If seed germination rate drops below 40% accompanied by collar constriction in emerging rows.
sources: ICAR-VPKAS Soil Health & Seed Pathology Guide

disorders_and_pests.conducive_weather: Sub-zero night temperatures, calm cloudless skies following a sunny day (radiation freeze)
disorders_and_pests.distinguishing_features: Water-soaked dark green/black translucent foliage immediately following morning thaw; crispy blackened shoot tips; no visible fungal mycelium or insect puncture marks; affects top exposed canopy while sheltered lower leaves remain green.
cultural_controls: Light evening furrow irrigation before an anticipated frost night: moist soil absorbs more heat during the day and re-radiates it slowly overnight compared to dry soil.
Erect windward thermal screens or plant broad beans as an upper-terrace wind barrier.
physical_controls: Cover terrace beds with thermal agrifleece or clean dry straw before sunset; remove or ventilate next morning once sun warms air above 4°C.
Avoid touching or disturbing frozen brittle plants until they have naturally thawed in morning light.
biological_controls: Foliar spray of seaweed extract (Ascophyllum nodosum) or potassium silicate 48 hours before cold waves to increase cellular sap osmotic pressure.
safe_treatments: Light sprinkler misting just before sunrise can release latent heat of fusion to prevent internal ice crystallization in leaves.
disorders_and_pests.escalation_criteria: If ground temperatures drop below -5°C for more than 4 consecutive nocturnal hours on potato foliage.
sources: FAO Mountain Agriculture & ICAR Cold Arid Agro-meteorology Studies

disorders_and_pests.conducive_weather: Continuous rains, poor drainage, flat terraces without exit spillways, heavy clay soil
disorders_and_pests.distinguishing_features: Uniform chlorotic pale yellowing of lower leaves moving upward; plants wilt despite wet soil because suffocated roots cannot uptake water; sour fermented odor when soil is probed; dark grey or black rotted root tips lacking root hairs.
cultural_controls: Install 15-20 cm contour drainage furrows with a gentle 0.5% grade directed toward safe stone spillways.
Incorporate coarse sand, gravel chips, and mature fibrous compost into sticky clay terraces.
Switch to ridged planting beds for sensitive root crops like potatoes and carrots.
physical_controls: Immediately dig relief exit trenches along the inner heel of the terrace to drain perched surface puddles away from crops.
Aerate the upper 3 cm of compacted crust with a hand hoe once soil dries enough not to smear.
biological_controls: Inoculation with mycorrhizal fungi (VAM) after drainage is restored to stimulate root regeneration.
safe_treatments: Foliar feed with diluted compost tea or liquid vermiwash to supply micronutrients bypassing damaged roots during recovery.
disorders_and_pests.escalation_criteria: If water stands pooled for >36 hours in cold temperatures, causing complete root necrosis.
sources: ICAR-VPKAS Almora Drainage & Terrace Engineering Research
